purpose: A deterministic REFERENCE computation for canonical bytes: every arithmetic path fixed at build time, one thread, a pinned userspace, run on a pinned software CPU so that the physical host does not choose the arithmetic. Reproducible -- not physically validated, not experimentally verified, not ground truth.
status: STAGED -- not the canonical corpus's backend; migrating the corpus to it needs separate owner authorization (directive 7, s.35)

patches.reason: OpenBLAS 0.3.31 exports openblas_set_threads_callback_function from every build but compiles it only for threaded ones, so a USE_THREAD=0 shared library fails its own link test; the patch compiles the setter -- a store nothing in a serial library reads -- into the serial build. It changes no arithmetic.

fp_policy.rounding: round-to-nearest-even: IEEE default, nothing in the stack sets another; checked at runtime (ties go to even)
fp_policy.fma_contraction: none: -ffp-contract=off in every C/C++/Fortran build, and the software CPU has no FMA unit
fp_policy.extended_precision: none for double arithmetic: x86-64 SSE2; x87 appears only in libm long-double paths
fp_policy.flush_to_zero: off: no -ffast-math anywhere, MXCSR default; checked at runtime (a subnormal survives)
fp_policy.libm: the rootfs's glibc libm, by its bytes; its IFUNCs select on the SOFTWARE CPU's CPUID, which offers no FMA or AVX
fp_policy.compiler_isa_baseline: OpenBLAS kernels for TARGET=NEHALEM; NumPy baseline X86_V2 with no runtime dispatch; no -march=native or -mtune=native anywhere
